minimal_one_turn_counterfactual.scope: Same observed state and same recorded opponent commands; no full-match causal claim

diagnosis.observed: Turn 10 moves our visible F from (6,7) downward while the two visible opposing F enter the plaza. One-line rightward replacement keeps the plaza neutral under the same recorded opposing action.
diagnosis.hypothesis: Dynamic greedy adversarial rollouts plus scalar state evaluation can prefer a path that sacrifices immediate F contest or early score to modeled future value. A stronger internal opponent is not necessarily a better calibrated opponent.
unresolved: Actual chosen continuation and four response values were not logged; cannot attribute this action to only the adversarial selector.
Common a_clean/post-evaluation deadline changes remain a confound.
The later economy and battle trajectory includes both players adapting after divergence, so the one-turn replacement is not evidence of a full-game win.

minimal_one_turn_counterfactual.scope: Same observed state and same recorded opponent commands; no full-match causal claim

diagnosis.observed: Turn 31 redirects exactly F1+W2 at (8,12) downward instead of upward. Resources, ownership and total units are initially unchanged, but replacing these two moves reproduces the v3 next snapshot exactly.
diagnosis.hypothesis: The different downside aggregation changes which local joint F/W direction is preferred; the resulting strategic route can lose economy despite similar immediate score and army totals. Lower-tail mean is not uniformly more conservative than the previous worst-value mixture.
unresolved: No recorded score vector proves that tail weighting alone caused the branch. Source comparison narrows the plausible causes but does not isolate time/cleanup effects.
No enemy within Manhattan distance 2 of (8,12) in the shared pre-state; the branch is not evidence of an immediate local forced retreat.
Later compound losses and economy differences cannot be assigned entirely to this one move without a fresh controlled replay experiment.
